## Design

### 2026-10-11 – After working on my Starbie PCB design video, I faced a huge problem in my finalised Starbie project. When i ran the project it started showing many errors that was outside my knowledge. To remove the

**5.32h**

After working on my Starbie PCB design video, I faced a huge problem in my finalised Starbie project. When i ran the project it started showing many errors that was outside my knowledge. To remove these errors, I spent additional time checking and improving the project. I reviewed the schematic connections between the XIAO ESP32-C3, buttons, OLED display, MPU6050 sensor and DHT11 sensor.

I also worked on assigning component footprints and fixing problems with the custom KiCad libraries. One issue was that the XIAO footprint's silkscreen overlapped solder-mask openings. I investigated the warnings and modified the footprint graphics, reducing the DRC warnings from 8 to one.

I ran the Design Rules Checker, checked the schematic against the PCB and confirmed that KiCad reported zero electrical errors and zero unconnected items. I exported the Gerber and drill files and opened them in Gerber Viewer to inspect the board.

The biggest challenge was learning the difference between schematic symbols, footprints and PCB layers. I now understand more about how a circuit becomes a physical board.

Next, I plan to verify component dimensions and pinouts, review the final design and prepare it for the next build stage.

### 2026-10-11 – For this session, I focused on improving my Starbie PCB and making sure everything was properly documented.

**4.02h**

For this session, I focused on improving my Starbie PCB and making sure everything was properly documented.

First 42  minutes: I reviewed the components in my schematic, checking the ESP32-C3 pin connections, OLED display, MPU6050 motion sensor, DHT11 sensor and buttons. I compared their pinouts and footprints to make sure the actual parts would fit and connect correctly.

![Screen Shot 2026-10-11 at 11.32.40 pm](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cBBK111nWIThGGVNKRtywaVwPwdRViXt/9575fa7ac2590809c97d510ef03a6f38733d0a8b3ed1ebdcdeb43adf14ea0f30.png)

Next 108 minutes: I worked on improving my GitHub repository. I updated the README with an explanation of how Starbie works in html as it was not letting me post it in normal text (which was really wierd for some reason but good thing i know coding atleast), the components I us ed, screenshots of my PCB and the challenges I faced while designing it. (Check out my readme, I feel like its to long but my friend said its normal)

![Screen Shot 2026-10-12 at 12.02.02 am](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cBBK111nWIThGGVNKRtywaVwPwdRViXt/7f9d3de59a8f278f9b79b2b08338e20988ff6f170f9111d0c13fcf109f4b6afe.png)

Next 39 minutes: I reviewed my Gerber files, PCB outline, copper layers and bill of materials. I also investigated the  remaining footprint-library mismatch warning and checked whether any corrections were needed.

![Screen Shot 2026-10-12 at 12.00.08 am](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cBBK111nWIThGGVNKRtywaVwPwdRViXt/952d6524234346491a8fd964d2fdfb9156ed721732d94defbf0525ab0a756c0d.png)

I also spent another 52 minutes designing a custom logo for Starbie because I wanted my PCB to look more unique and personal. I experimented with different designs, sizes and placements to find something that suited the project. I also had to consider how the logo would look on the actual PCB without interfering with the components or tracks. It honestly took longer than I expected just to make a small logo, but I enjoyed being able to add something creative to the project after spending so much time on the technical side. I'm happy with how it turned out, and it makes Starbie feel more like my own creation. (BTW I LOVE ART)

![Screen Shot 2026-10-11 at 11.58.51 pm](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cBBK111nWIThGGVNKRtywaVwPwdRViXt/e958cdf6261558be08e4ab58a4d8f768b1f009057555b508ddb9beabb5c73e20.png)

This session helped me understand that designing a PCB isn't just about connecting components. It's also about making sure the physical parts will fit, checking for manufacturing problems and documenting the design properly.

![Screen Shot 2026-10-11 at 10.28.02 pm](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cBBK111nWIThGGVNKRtywaVwPwdRViXt/fcc43e3005eb2126f6f5d6751fe712472f7137344b39dd7c94bb5a4005a1819d.png)
My next goal is to get the PCB design approved so I can eventually build and test Starbie!
